# Cycle C01 — Written proofs

Conventions. Σ is a finite alphabet with q ≥ 1 symbols; words are elements of
the free monoid Σ*; |w| is the length (a meta-level notion). For a word w,
Borders(w) is the set of words b with 0 < |b| < |w| that are both a prefix and a
suffix of w. The autocorrelation polynomial of w (|w| = k) is
c_w(x) = 1 + Σ_{b ∈ Borders(w)} x^{k−|b|}.

---

## Theorem 1 (CLM-C01-01) — counting is the complete invariant of commutation

*Statement.* Let ≡ be the congruence on Σ* generated by ab = ba (a, b ∈ Σ).
Then u ≡ v iff for every symbol s, u and v contain s equally often; equivalently
iff the projections π_s(u), π_s(v) (delete all symbols except s) are equal.
Each projection is a word s…s ("unary numeral").

*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean: `Infinity.C01.commEq_iff_count`,
`Infinity.C01.projection_is_unary` (`proofs/lean/Infinity/C01_Quantity.lean`).
Outline: one swap step is a permutation, and permutations are generated by
adjacent swaps in context (Lean's inductive `List.Perm`), so ≡ is exactly the
permutation relation; permutations are characterised by symbol counts. ∎

---

## Theorem 2 (CLM-C01-02) — one symbol, one relation: index and period

*Statement.* On {a}*, identify a^x with x. Let ≡ be the congruence generated by
a^m = a^{m+p}, p ≥ 1. Then a^x ≡ a^y iff nf(x) = nf(y), where
nf(x) = x if x < m and nf(x) = m + ((x − m) mod p) otherwise. There are exactly
m + p classes, represented by a^0, …, a^{m+p−1}.

*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean: `gen_iff`, `exactly_m_add_p_classes`. ∎

---

## Theorem 3 (CLM-C01-03) — one symbol, several relations

*Statement.* Let R = {(m_i, n_i)}_{i=1..r} with m_i < n_i, d_i = n_i − m_i,
M = min m_i, P = gcd(d_1, …, d_r). The congruence ≡ on {a}* generated by the
relations a^{m_i} = a^{n_i} satisfies: a^x ≡ a^y iff x = y or (x, y ≥ M and
P divides x − y). It has exactly M + P classes.

*Proof.* Work in (N, +). Let E = {(x, y) : x = y, or x, y ≥ M and P | x − y}.

(≡ ⊆ E). E is an equivalence relation; it is compatible with addition (if
x E y then (x+k) E (y+k)); and every generating pair (m_i, n_i) lies in E
(both ≥ M, difference d_i divisible by P). Since ≡ is the smallest such
relation, ≡ ⊆ E.

(E ⊆ ≡). *Step 1.* For every j and every x ≥ m_j, x ≡ x + d_j (shift the
relation m_j ≡ n_j by x − m_j). Iterating, x ≡ x + t·d_j for all t ≥ 0 (all
intermediate values stay ≥ m_j).
*Step 2.* Let L = max m_j. Since P = gcd(d_j), there are integers c_j with
Σ c_j d_j = P; put α_j = max(c_j, 0), β_j = max(−c_j, 0), so
Σ α_j d_j = P + Σ β_j d_j =: S. For x ≥ L, Step 1 (applied for each j in turn;
all intermediate values are ≥ L ≥ m_j) gives x ≡ x + S and x + P ≡ x + P + Σ β_j d_j = x + S.
Hence x ≡ x + P for all x ≥ L.
*Step 3.* Let i₀ with m_{i₀} = M, and let x ≥ M. Choose t with x + t·d_{i₀} ≥ L.
By Step 1, x ≡ x + t·d_{i₀} and x + P ≡ x + P + t·d_{i₀}; by Step 2,
x + t·d_{i₀} ≡ x + t·d_{i₀} + P. Therefore x ≡ x + P for every x ≥ M, and by
induction x ≡ x + rP for r ≥ 0. If x, y ≥ M and P | x − y, then x ≡ y.

Counting: the singletons {0}, …, {M−1} and the P residue classes of [M, ∞)
give M + P classes. ∎

*Computational corroboration.* EXP-C01-02: 6159 relation sets, two independent
methods (Knuth–Bendix completion; bounded union–find), 0 disagreements.

## Theorem 4 (CLM-C01-04) — multiplication as composition of transformations

*Statement.* Let End({a}*) be the set of monoid endomorphisms of {a}*. With
(φ ⊕ ψ)(w) = φ(w)ψ(w) and composition ∘, (End({a}*), ⊕, ∘) is a commutative
semiring and φ ↦ |φ(a)| is an isomorphism onto (N, +, ·). For two symbols
modulo commutation, the endomorphism monoid under composition is not
commutative.

*Proof.* An endomorphism is determined by φ(a) = a^k; write φ_k. Then
φ_k(a^n) = a^{kn}. Since {a}* is commutative, φ_k ⊕ φ_l is again an
endomorphism: (φ_k ⊕ φ_l)(uv) = φ_k(u)φ_k(v)φ_l(u)φ_l(v) =
φ_k(u)φ_l(u)φ_k(v)φ_l(v); and (φ_k ⊕ φ_l)(a) = a^{k+l}, (φ_k ∘ φ_l)(a) =
φ_k(a^l) = a^{kl}. So k ↦ φ_k is a bijection N → End({a}*) carrying + to ⊕ and
· to ∘; all semiring laws transfer from N (or are checked directly: EXP-C01-03).
For {a, b} modulo commutation (≅ N²), let φ(a) = φ(b) = b and ψ(a) = ψ(b) = a.
Then (φ∘ψ)(a) = φ(a) = b while (ψ∘φ)(a) = ψ(b) = a. ∎

## Refutation (CLM-C01-05) — a single rearranging relation does not generate counting equivalence

*Statement refuted (H-C01-4).* "For every relation u ↔ v over {a,b} with u ≠ v
and equal symbol counts, the generated congruence equals counting (Parikh)
equivalence on all words of length ≥ |u|."

*Counterexample.* u = aab, v = aba. The only words of length 3 containing a
factor aab or aba are aab and aba, so baa is fixed by every rewrite and its
class is {baa}, while aab, aba, baa have equal symbol counts. (EXP-C01-04
finds a counterexample for each of the 33 relations of length 3 and 4.) ∎

## Theorem 5 (CLM-C01-06) — the border-containment theorem

*Statement.* Let u ≠ v ∈ Σ^k with Borders(u) ⊆ Borders(v), and let ~ be the
congruence generated by u = v. Then

1. the rewriting system R = {u → v} is terminating and confluent;
2. the classes of ~ on Σ^n are in bijection with the words of length n that do
   not contain u as a factor;
3. Σ_{n≥0} |Σ^n/~| x^n = c_u(x) / (x^k + (1 − q x) c_u(x)).

In particular, if u is unbordered the generating function is
1/(1 − q x + x^k); for q = 2 this is 1/((1 − x)(1 − x − … − x^{k−1})), the
partial sums of the (k−1)-bonacci numbers (k = 3: F(n+3) − 1).

*Proof.* (1) *Termination.* A step x u y → x v y preserves length, so every
derivation from w stays in the finite set Σ^{|w|}. Let t be the first position
where u and v differ; every step changes the word first at offset |x| + t, from
u_t to v_t. Hence all steps move strictly in the same direction of the
lexicographic order of Σ^{|w|} (increasing if u_t < v_t, decreasing otherwise),
so no derivation is longer than q^{|w|}.

*Local confluence.* Let w → w₁ and w → w₂ rewrite occurrences of u at
positions i ≤ j. If i = j, w₁ = w₂. If j ≥ i + k, the occurrences are disjoint
and rewriting the other occurrence in each of w₁, w₂ gives a common word. If
i < j < i + k, put d = j − i and b = w[j, i+k) — the overlap. Since both
occurrences spell u, b is a suffix of u (from the first occurrence) and a
prefix of u (from the second), so b ∈ Borders(u), and
u = p b = b s with |p| = |s| = d. By hypothesis b ∈ Borders(v): v = p′b = b s′.
Writing w = x p b s y: w₁ = x v s y and w₂ = x p v y. By the lemma
`common_border_joinable` (Lean), v s = p′u, p v = u s′ and p′v = v s′, so
w₁ = x p′ u y → x p′ v y and w₂ = x u s′ y → x v s′ y = x p′ v y.
Thus R is locally confluent; with termination, Newman's lemma gives confluence.

(2) For a convergent system, each ↔*_R class contains exactly one irreducible
word; ↔*_R is the congruence generated by u = v; irreducible words are those
avoiding u; and classes respect length.

(3) The number of length-n words over a q-letter alphabet avoiding u has
generating function c_u(x)/(x^k + (1 − q x)c_u(x)) (Guibas–Odlyzko 1981,
"String overlaps, pattern matching, and nontransitive games", JCTA 30).
For unbordered u, c_u = 1, and 1 − 2x + x^k = (1 − x)(1 − x − … − x^{k−1}). ∎

*Corroboration.* EXP-C01-05: 756 relations with an unbordered side, 0
failures; EXP-C01-06/07: all 1632 containment-or-completion cases agree.

## Theorem 6 (CLM-C01-07) — computer-assisted proofs for 1632 specific relations

*Statement.* For each of the 1632 relations marked PROVEN in
`results/EXP-C01-07.json` (binary k ≤ 6, ternary k ≤ 4), the class-count
generating function equals c(x)/(x^k + (1 − q x)c(x)) with c the common-border
polynomial of Conjecture 7.

*Proof (computer-assisted).* For each relation the program finds, for some
shortlex order, a finite rule set R′ produced by Knuth–Bendix completion from
u = v (so every rule of R′ is a consequence of u = v), and then *independently
re-verifies* that (a) each rule is shortlex-decreasing (termination), (b) every
critical pair of R′ is joinable (local confluence; Newman ⇒ confluence), and
(c) u and v have the same R′-normal form (so R′ generates exactly the
congruence of u = v). Then the classes of Σ^n correspond to R′-irreducible
words, which are the words accepted by the Aho–Corasick automaton of the
left-hand sides, with s live states. The count sequence a_n therefore
satisfies a linear recurrence of order ≤ s (Cayley–Hamilton), and the
predicted sequence b_n one of order ≤ k (denominator of degree k, numerator of
degree < k). Hence a − b satisfies a recurrence of order ≤ s + k, and equality
of the first s + k + 5 terms (checked) implies a_n = b_n for all n. As a guard
against implementation errors the automaton counts are also compared with
brute-force union–find class counts for n ≤ 8 (all agree). ∎

*Trust base.* The Python implementation of completion verification, the
automaton and exact integer arithmetic (not machine-checked in Lean).

## Conjecture 7 (CLM-C01-08) — the common-border formula

*Statement.* For all u ≠ v ∈ Σ^k (q = |Σ|),
Σ_n |Σ^n/~| x^n = c(x)/(x^k + (1 − q x) c(x)), where
c(x) = 1 + Σ_{b ∈ Borders(u) ∩ Borders(v)} x^{k−|b|}.

*Status.* Proved when Borders(u) ⊆ Borders(v) or vice versa (Theorem 5) and
for 1632 individual relations (Theorem 6); verified for all 2159 relations with
binary k ≤ 6 / ternary k ≤ 4 up to n = 12 (binary) and n = 7 (ternary)
(EXP-C01-06); open in general. The open cases have infinite (but apparently
regular) completions, e.g. aba ↔ bab completes to bab → aba together with
b a^j b a → a b a a b^{j−1} (j ≥ 2).

*Proof idea under investigation.* Interpret the class-count series as the
Hilbert series of K⟨Σ⟩/(u − v) and show that only overlaps along common
borders contribute "chains" (in the sense of Anick's resolution); overlaps
along non-common borders produce Gröbner-basis elements whose own overlaps
cancel in the Euler characteristic.
